models.description: The east gate of Seoul's Joseon city wall (pavilion 1869): a granite base with one arched passage under a two-storey pavilion with double hipped roofs, wrapped in front by its semicircular crenellated ongseong.
The throne hall of Changdeokgung (rebuilt 1804): a double hipped-and-gabled roof over ochre lattice, on a plain two-tier stone platform.

The main hall of Jogyesa (1938), head temple of the Jogye Order: a tall single-storey hall of 7 × 4 bays with green lattice doors between red columns under a huge hipped-and-gabled roof, the order's emblem on its gables.

The main hall of Jongmyo, the Joseon royal ancestral shrine: 19 bays of red columns and plank doors under one long, low gabled roof, with its lower end rooms and the two wings turning forward, on its stone terrace.
